generatedCommentsNodes.comment: In the test method `testDuplicateSliceRelease`, there is a typo in the assertion: `buf.duplicate().duplicate()` should likely be `buf.duplicate().slice()`. This will ensure that the test checks the intended behavior of slicing a duplicated buffer.

The removal of the `duplicate()` and `slice(int index, int length)` methods from `ReadOnlyUnsafeDirectByteBuf` and their replacement with new classes (`ReadOnlySlicedByteBuf` and `ReadOnlyDuplicatedByteBuf`) in `ReadOnlyByteBufferBuf` is inconsistent. The same pattern should be applied to all read-only buffer implementations for consistency.

The introduction of `ReadOnlySlicedByteBuf` and `ReadOnlyDuplicatedByteBuf` with overridden methods that return new instances of themselves can lead to a proliferation of similar classes, making the codebase harder to maintain. Consider using composition or a factory pattern to manage these variations more efficiently.

review_comment: The reason why read-only ByteBuffers are needed in the SslHandler use case is to avoid mutating the buffer. JDK's SSLEngine will mutate the input buffer with an in-place encryption reusing the input buffer unless the buffer is read-only. The support for read-only ByteBuffers in JDK's SSLEngine was added as a result of a bug reported by @chrisvest, more details in comment https://github.com/netty/netty/issues/14069#issuecomment-2129279047 .
